 Rep. Meng reintroduces legislation to make Diwali a federal holiday
 By Shane O’Brien 
 … Comments 
 Posted on November 10, 2026 
 U.S. Rep. Grace Meng has reintroduced legislation that would make Diwali a federal holiday. Photo courtesy of the Office of Rep. Grace Meng 
 U.S. Rep. Grace Meng has reintroduced legislation to make Diwali a federal holiday in the United States amid a sharp uptick in anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate across the United States.
 Meng, the chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus, reintroduced the legislation on Monday, one day after the main celebration of the 2026 Diwali festival on Sunday.
 Under Meng’s legislation, which currently has 19 co-sponsors in Congress, Diwali would become the 12th federally recognized holiday in the United States. She said establishing Diwali as a federal holiday and creating a day off would allow communities of Hindus, Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists to celebrate it. The legislation would also serve as a signal that government values their cultures and traditions at a time of rising anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate, Meng added.
 “At a time when anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate is on the rise, recognizing Diwali as a federal holiday sends a powerful message that Hindus, as well as Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists, are valued members of our society,” Meng said in a statement. “Here in Queens, I see firsthand how meaningful Diwali is to so many families and communities.
 “My Diwali Day Act will help educate Americans about the importance of this day, and I will continue working to create a more inclusive nation that honors the rich cultural traditions of its people.”
 Diwali, also known as Deepavali or the Festival of Lights, is one of the most important holidays of the year for many religious groups and celebrates the victory of good over evil, light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance.
 Meng pointed to a rise in anti-Hindu hate across the United States, stating that Hindu and South Asian communities are facing an alarming rise in hate, intimidation and targeted violence, including vandalism at Hindu places of worship and an attempted mass shooting at Navratri festivities at a Hindu temple in Illinois in October.
 Alexandros Paporakis, a 19-year-0ld college student who attempted to carry the massacre at the Sri Venkateswara Swami Temple in Aurora, has been charged with felony counts of making a terrorist threat and unlawful possession of a rifle. Paporakis’s attempts to carry out the massacre were thwarted only by his gun jamming, according to reports.
 Meanwhile, research conducted by Santa Clara University’s Center for the Study of Organized Hate found that anti-South Asian hate speech was 240% higher on social media platform X between January 2025 and June 2026 than it was in January 2024.
 Meng, who has also authorized a Lunar New Year Day Act that would make Lunar New Year a federal holiday, said the Diwali Day legislation would help combat rising anti-South Asian hate by creating a more inclusive nation that honors the traditions and cultures of its communities.
 The legislation is endorsed by a number of advocacy groups, including Asian Americans Advancing Justice (AAJC), Asian American Federation (AAF), Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA), Hindus for Human Rights and over a dozen more.
 Meng last introduced legislation to make Diwali a federal holiday in 2023, which was referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability. However, the legislation did not advance further before the end of the congressional session.
